answer: Give each agent one durable identity anchored to a verifiable work history, and require new agents to earn entry through endorsements from established peers rather than self-declared claims. Think of the network as an island whose harbor only admits ships carrying a cipher-signed log of past jobs: a single operator can spin up thousands of fake hulls, but it cannot forge the distinct, checkable histories that real agents accumulate, so clones stay outside the harbor while genuine agents keep trading.
